Deep-Fried Khapse Pastries

Served at: Losar (Tibetan New Year)

Makes about 30-40 pieces, depending on sizePrep 45 minCook 30 min

Khapse are traditional Tibetan fried cookies or biscuits, a staple during Losar, the Tibetan New Year. These crispy, often intricately shaped pastries symbolize prosperity and good fortune, adorning altars and shared generously among family and friends to celebrate new beginnings and blessings.

Ingredients

  • 4 cups (480g) all-purpose flour, plus more for dusting
  • 1/2 cup (100g) granulated sugar
  • 1 teaspoon baking powder
  • 1/2 teaspoon salt
  • 1/2 cup (113g) unsalted butter, melted, or vegetable oil
  • 1 cup (240ml) milk or water, warmed, plus more if needed
  • 6-8 cups (1.5-2 liters) vegetable oil, for deep frying

Method

  1. In a large mixing bowl, whisk together the flour, granulated sugar, baking powder, and salt.
  2. Pour the melted butter or vegetable oil into the dry ingredients and mix with your hands until the mixture resembles coarse crumbs.
  3. Gradually add the warm milk or water, mixing until a shaggy dough forms. Continue to knead the dough in the bowl or on a lightly floured surface for about 5-7 minutes, until it is smooth and elastic. If the dough is too dry, add a tablespoon of milk at a time; if too sticky, add a tablespoon of flour.
  4. Cover the dough with a clean kitchen towel and let it rest at room temperature for at least 30 minutes.
  5. Divide the dough into 3-4 equal portions. On a lightly floured surface, roll out one portion of dough to about 1/8-inch (3mm) thickness.
  6. Using a knife or pastry wheel, cut the dough into desired shapes. Traditional shapes include long strips, diamond shapes, or braided pieces. For braids, cut strips about 1 inch (2.5 cm) wide and 6 inches (15 cm) long, make a slit in the middle, and pull one end through the slit to create a twist.
  7. Heat the vegetable oil in a large, heavy-bottomed pot or deep fryer to 350°F (175°C).
  8. Carefully place a few khapse pieces into the hot oil, ensuring not to overcrowd the pot. Fry for 2-3 minutes per side, or until golden brown and puffed.
  9. Using a slotted spoon, remove the fried khapse and place them on a wire rack lined with paper towels to drain excess oil.
  10. Repeat with the remaining dough, rolling and frying in batches.
  11. Allow the khapse to cool completely before serving or storing.

Tips

  • Maintain a consistent oil temperature; if it's too low, khapse will be greasy, and if too high, they will burn quickly on the outside and remain raw inside.
  • For a richer flavor, you can substitute some of the milk with evaporated milk or add a pinch of ground cardamom to the dough.
  • Store cooled khapse in an airtight container at room temperature for up to two weeks, making them perfect for preparing ahead of Losar celebrations.
